runner.proxy_note: Optional HTTP(S) proxy for commands that need Internet access (git clone, pip/apt, downloading reference repos). Set http/https on the runner that actually reaches the Internet; leave "" to run direct. When set, run.sh always exports http_proxy/https_proxy (+ upper-case) and no_proxy for every command on that runner.
runner.env_note: Optional extra environment variables applied to EVERY command on the runner, as a list of "KEY=VALUE" strings (e.g. "ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu", "HF_HOME=/scratch/hf"). Values are shell-quoted, so spaces/special chars are safe over SSH. Exported last, so they override tool/proxy defaults.

benchmark.e2e_cases_note: Optional. If the project has multiple e2e test cases / workloads (different drivers, model configs, or input scenarios), list them as {"name", "cmd", "weight"}. integrate requires EVERY case to pass; profile-e2e sums weighted per-kernel wall-clock across all cases into ONE ranking; the report shows per-case baseline->final + a geomean. Empty = single default workload.

integration.note: Last-mile backend integration policy (skill: sycl-integration). The goal of a migration is a fully functional SYCL/XPU backend of the project — its own build, its own runtime, its own entrypoint — not a standalone kernel layer. Depth is measured as a Backend Readiness Level: L0 kernel-standalone, L1 build-through, L2 runtime-live (project's own test suite passes), L3 workload-correct (the real workload runs and matches a reference — the level required to claim 'runs on Intel GPU'), L4 workload-fast (measured e2e baseline->final speedup).
integration.target_level_note: Optional user override of the level the agent commits to reaching. Empty = the agent decides at `scaffold` from the project archetype and records the reason. Set e.g. "L3" to require the real workload to run correctly, or "L1" to deliberately scope integration down.
integration.archetype_note: Optional hint: A=C/C++ app with a backend seam, B=C++ library+CMake+own tests, C=framework custom-op extension (PyTorch/TF), D=Python array/JIT library, E=runtime/JIT-codegen system, F=graph/parser-driven engine. Empty = the agent classifies it.
integration.backend_switch_note: Optional: how the SYCL/XPU backend should be selected (e.g. "cmake -DFOO_ENABLE_SYCL=ON", "make BACKEND=sycl", "device='xpu'"). Empty = the agent designs the switch and records it.
integration.build_command_note: Optional: the project's OWN build command with the SYCL backend enabled. This is the L1 gate — a test binary does not count. Empty = the agent derives it from the build system.
integration.suite_command_note: Optional: the project's OWN test suite command with the backend selected (ctest / pytest / make test). This is the L2 gate. Empty = the agent discovers it.
integration.workload_reference: Same llama-cli invocation with -ngl 0 (CPU backend), same seed and --temp 0: greedy-decoded token sequence must match. Secondary: llama-perplexity on wiki.test.raw, SYCL ppl within 0.5% of CPU ppl.
integration.workload_reference_note: Optional: what the end-to-end workload output must be compared against for L3 (a reference artifact path, a golden output, an accuracy metric + target). Empty = the agent picks the best available and records which, per sycl-integration/references/e2e-validation.md.

guardrails.note: Optional behavioral guardrails for LLM engines that misbehave in specific ways. Each is OPT-IN and independently toggleable — enable only for engines that exhibit the problem, disable for engines you already trust. The agent reads this block on start and obeys it for the whole run. These guardrails may tighten behavior but never relax the framework's correctness/commit/log guarantees.

gpu_hang_recovery.note: Safe recovery when a build/test/profile/bench process hangs on the GPU. When ON, the agent may ONLY try to terminate the offending process (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL, including its child/descendant PIDs). It must NEVER touch the GPU driver or device to unstick a hang: no kernel-module reload (rmmod/modprobe i915/xe/drm), no GPU or FLR reset, no `xpu-smi`/`intel_gpu_reset` device reset, no host reboot — a failed reset can wedge the entire host. If the process cannot be killed, STOP and report a blocker with the hung PID and last command; do NOT escalate to any driver/device-level action. Disable (false) only for engines you trust to handle hangs safely on their own.

gpu_concurrency.note: Serialize GPU-bound commands so only one build/test/profile/bench/exec runs on the GPU at a time. Multiple agents/subagents can invoke run.sh concurrently; the lock makes them wait rather than overload a single GPU, which is the most common cause of unrecoverable hangs/crashes. The lock lives on the RUNNER (remote workdir when mode=remote, .sycl/ when local). Non-GPU verbs (env/setup/sync/pull) are never locked. Disable only if you are certain no concurrent invocations can reach the same GPU.

no_lazy_completion.note: Forbid 'lazy' early exit, seen on some engines that quit once the easy work is done. When ON, the agent MUST migrate/optimize EVERY non-skipped kernel and drive every workflow step through to `report`. It may NOT skip a kernel because it looks low-priority, complex, risky, or time-consuming (difficulty is never a skip reason — only dead code / not-a-kernel / explicit user exclusion are), and may NOT stop mid-workflow except for the documented legitimate stops (platform-mismatch halt, a genuine unresolvable blocker, or an explicit user review gate). Disable (false) only for engines that already run to completion reliably.

review.note: Phase-exit review policy (skill: sycl-review, state: state/phases.json). Every phase is entered with `evidence.sh enter <phase>` and left with `evidence.sh gate <phase>`, which checks that phase's exit criteria and is the only thing that may mark it exited. This exists because the evidence checks E1-E14 can only falsify a claim that was made — they are blind to a phase that was skipped in silence, which is the most common way a migration ships incomplete while auditing clean.
review.hotspot_pct_threshold_note: A kernel at or above this share of end-to-end wall-clock must have a measured optimization trial OR a recorded reason for having none before `optimize` can close. A trial that was measured, ineffective and reverted counts — the criterion is whether the question was asked. Raising this to dodge a gate invalidates the comparison; lower it to demand more.
review.max_gate_attempts_note: How many times a failing gate may be refined and re-run before the agent stops, records the unmet criteria as a blocker and moves on. Looping on one boundary spends the budget the remaining phases need.
review.fresh_context_subagent_note: Run the phase review in a fresh subagent context. The point of the review is to look at the phase WITHOUT the reasoning that produced it; an agent reviewing its own working context mostly re-derives its own conclusions.

targets.note: SYCL target style for migrated kernels. Default is plain hand-written SYCL 2020. sycl-tla is a CUTLASS-style header-only tile library reserved for XMX-bound tiled tensor algebra (GEMM/attention); see framework skill sycl-reference/references/sycl-tla-patterns.md for the decision rule.

sycl_tla.note: Header-only; add this include dir to the SYCL build. Leave "" to fall back to the reference_repos 'sycl-tla' path.

reference_repos.note: Local upstream repos the agent may consult (read-only) for how real Intel-GPU SYCL code is written. Toggle each repo with its own "enabled" flag (top-level "enabled" gates them all). Set path to "" or "enabled": false to disable one. Absolute paths on the machine that runs the agent. The agent extracts patterns/approaches only — it never copies code verbatim (respect upstream licenses). The installer can clone missing enabled repos on demand using each entry's "url" (empty url = not auto-clonable; leave/edit "path" manually).

repos.name: oneDNN
repos.use: Production Intel-GPU SYCL/oneAPI primitives (GEMM, conv, reorder, softmax, norm): blocking, sub-group + XMX/DPAS usage, memory layouts.

repos.name: sycl-tla
repos.use: CUTLASS-style tiled tensor algebra for Intel GPU: high-performance GEMM/attention tiling, joint_matrix (XMX) templates.

repos.name: intel-llvm
repos.use: DPC++ compiler + SYCL runtime/headers: authoritative SYCL 2020 API semantics and sycl::ext::oneapi::* extensions (sub-group, joint_matrix, bfloat16).

repos.name: igc
repos.use: Intel Graphics Compiler: how SYCL/SPIR-V lowers to Xe ISA, built-in/intrinsic behavior, codegen constraints.

repos.name: compute-runtime
repos.use: Level-Zero/OpenCL GPU driver (NEO): device limits, allocation/USM behavior, queue/submission semantics.

repos.name: pytorch
repos.use: ATen XPU SYCL kernels (aten/src/ATen/native/xpu, c10/xpu): elementwise, reduction, indexing, normalization on Intel GPU.

repos.name: vllm-xpu
repos.use: vLLM Intel-GPU backend: attention, paged KV-cache, sampling — end-to-end LLM-serving kernel structure on XPU.

repos.name: vllm-xpu-kernels
repos.use: Standalone high-performance SYCL kernels for vLLM XPU: attention, quantization, MoE — concrete kernel examples.

repos.name: intel-xpu-backend-for-triton
repos.use: Triton Intel-GPU backend: SPIR-V/Xe lowering, block pointers, DPAS tiling — codegen + optimization patterns.

repos.name: metrics-library
repos.use: Intel Metrics Library: GPU performance-counter programming — semantics of profiling metrics.

repos.name: metrics-discovery
repos.use: Metrics Discovery API: enumerates HW metrics/counters — meaning of counters surfaced by the profiler.

repos.name: oneMKL
repos.use: oneAPI Math Kernel Library (oneMKL) interfaces: BLAS, LAPACK, RNG, FFT SYCL implementations and domain APIs for Intel GPU.

repos.name: oneDPL
repos.use: oneAPI DPC++ Library (oneDPL): parallel algorithms, iterators, and execution policies for SYCL — patterns for reductions, scans, sorts, transforms.
